results.title: CrowdStrike blames mismatch in Falcon sensor update for global IT outage | Cybersecurity Dive
results.content: # CrowdStrike blames mismatch in Falcon sensor update for global IT outage. The security company, in its root cause analysis report, said it is using lessons from the crash to make larger changes, while analysts predict further challenges. * A mismatched software update in CrowdStrike's Falcon sensor led to the crash that caused a global IT outage of millions of Microsoft Windows systems on July 19, the company said Tuesday. * CrowdStrike, in a root cause analysis report, said the Falcon sensor expected 20 input fields in a rapid response content update, but the software update actually provided 21 input fields. * “We are using lessons learned from this incident to better serve our customers,” CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement Tuesday. CrowdStrike said it has already begun to make significant process changes to make sure such a catastrophic update will not take place in the future. The incident will likely lead CrowdStrike to enact significant changes in its design and development processes, and additional changes that could impact corporate governance. “It is likely CrowdStrike is evaluating potential architectural changes to the sensor, future direction and overhaul for [quality assurance] and how to approach the market to rebuild trust.”. Federal officials said the CrowdStrike incident will make them redouble efforts to crack down on memory unsafe code, which has been a longstanding problem in connection to recent security vulnerabilities. Asked about whether the incident could impact its coding practices, CrowdStrike noted limitations to what it could change in order to remain compatible with specific operating systems. “As Microsoft itself outlined on its security blog, security products in the Windows ecosystem, including the Falcon sensor, commonly leverage kernel drivers as core components of a robust security offering,” a CrowdStrike spokesperson said via email. “The kernel-mode parts of CrowdStrike Falcon’s sensor, like other software that runs in the kernel of the Windows operating system, must be written in C/C++ language, which does not allow for memory-safe coding.”. The carrier last week hired famed attorney David Boies and said it would seek damages for the incident, but CrowdStrike and Microsoft pushed back questioning why Delta had so many more issues compared to other airlines.

results.title: Duplex mismatch - Wikipedia
results.content: On an Ethernet connection, a **duplex mismatch** is a condition where two connected devices operate in different duplex modes "Duplex (telecommunications)"), that is, one operates in half duplex while the other one operates in full duplex. Duplex mismatch may be caused by manually setting two connected network interfaces at different duplex modes or by connecting a device that performs autonegotiation to one that is manually set to a full duplex mode. Therefore, the autonegotiating end of the connection uses half duplex while the non-negotiating peer is locked at full duplex, and this is a duplex mismatch. A duplex mismatch causes problems when both ends of the connection attempt to transfer data at the same time. If there is no option but to have a locked setting on one end and autonegotiation on the other (for example, an old device with broken autonegotiation connected to an unmanaged switch), half duplex must be used.

results.title: Effect of moderate learning style–teaching mode mismatch ...
results.content: This study tried to tackle that controversy by comparing and assessing the effect of different learning styles on performance in physiology examination when teaching mode was somewhat different than learning preferences of the 2 nd year medical students. Frequency of preferred teaching modes among different learning styles Open in a new tab The results of this study indicate that learning and teaching mismatch does not result in any significant academic failures in medical education since all the students scored above 60% and activists and reflectors had almost the same results. It was thought earlier that a mismatch in learning style and teaching mode results in frustration and learning failure,[4,5] but recently, many studies indicate that a moderate mismatch does not leave students and teachers unhappy rather it strengthens student–teacher interaction and encourages the development of new learning skills.[2,6,7] A mismatch in medical education still remains uncharacterized. In another study, with mismatched teaching and learning, theorists had slightly higher scores than the rest of the three learning styles, and this finding supports our results.[9] The study also found that the scores of different learning styles were not statistically different, and hence academic performance is independent of moderate learning style–teaching mode mismatch.[9] In this study, we found significant differences in the scores of theorist and pragmatist styles of learning as compared to activist and reflector styles of learning, which is contradictory to both of the above researches and can be due to the reason that “examination style” or “teaching modes” in this study were different from the above researches. who found significant differences in learning styles of males and females.[15] In this study, problem-based learning sessions were the most preferred mode of teaching among the students. This result is supported by Novak _et al_.[16] and contradicted by Costa _et al_.[17] and Carrier _et al_.[18] Self-study sessions were the least preferred mode of teaching in our study which is contradicted by Mukhtar _et al_.[19] ### Limitations Our study is limited by the fact that the mismatch in learning and teaching in this study was not compared with an environment where there is complete learning style and teaching mode match. This study demonstrated that the effect on academic performance due to moderate mismatch in teaching mode and learning style is different for different types of learners.
